title: Dutch law adopts the Electronic Bill of Lading
subtitle: A change in Dutch law has, for the first time, given an electronic bill of lading the same legal force as its centuries-old paper original: the same proof of what was shipped, who owns it, and who may claim it. It is a quiet but foundational step for digital trade, and it lines up closely with the trusted digital product passports we help build.
featuredImageAlt: A faceted, low-poly illustration of a container cargo ship at sea in saturated teal, magenta and orange, overlaid with a glowing digital network mesh across the sky, representing the electronic bill of lading as a digital twin of physical cargo
excerpt: From 1 July 2026 the electronic bill of lading is legally binding in the Netherlands, given the same force as the centuries-old paper document. It is the first binding Dutch instance of a legally authoritative electronic transferable record, with a trust model (integrity, authenticity, control-as-possession, singularity) that maps almost line by line onto what a trustworthy Digital Product Passport needs, and it feeds directly into the trusted-DPP work we do in the TruPASS consortium and across our Brazil-Netherlands projects.
